newsitem.title: USA: Colorado police reopen high-profile murder case.
newsitem.headline: Colorado police reopen high-profile murder case.

text.p: An investigation into the 1983 murder of a college student who was the boyfriend of Robert Redford's daughter has been reopened, police said Friday.
Sidney Wells, 22, was a student at the Univeristy of Colorado in Boulder when he was found shot to death in his apartment on Aug. 1, 1983.
His roommate, Thayne Alan Smika, was arrested for the murder. No charges were filed at the time, but police want to talk to Smika again.
Boulder police believe Smika, who fled their jurisdiction, has changed his name and established a new identity in an unknown location.
Detective Melissa Hickman told a news conference that Boulder police were awaiting results on items submitted for additional testing to the FBI crime laboratory in Washington.

She said there was an active warrant out for Smika's arrest on forgery charges stemming from an alleged embezzlement in 1986 in Denver. "Mr. Smika is also wanted for further questioning in the murder of Sidney Wells," she said.
Wells, a journalism student, was dating Redford's daughter Shauna, who lived downstairs from him in an apartment building a few blocks from the university.
Redford who was in Buffalo, New York, at the time filming "The Natural," a film about baseball, closed down production to attend the funeral.
Police said Friday advances in the examination of forensic evidence allowed for testing that was not possible in 1983 but declined to give specifics.
